definition: Extension neural network is a pattern recognition method found by M.
details: H. Wang and C. P. Hung in 2003 to classify instances of data sets. Extension neural network is composed of artificial neural network and extension theory concepts. It uses the fast and adaptive learning capability of neural network and correlation estimation property of extension theory by calculating extension distance. ENN was used in: Failure detection in machinery. Tissue classification through MRI. Fault recognition in automotive engine. State of charge estimation in lead-acid battery. Classification with incomplete survey data.

explainer.lead: An extension neural network, or ENN, is a pattern-recognition architecture that combines an artificial neural network with extension theory to classify data. It pairs adaptive learning with extension distance, a way of estimating how an instance relates to possible classes.

tiers.eli5: Imagine learning to sort tools by looking at examples, then using a special measuring stick to decide where each new tool belongs. An extension neural network learns from data like other neural networks, but its measuring stick comes from extension theory. This helps it sort things such as tissue images or engine conditions into categories.
tiers.practitioner: An ENN can be applied as a classifier by learning patterns from a data set and then using extension distance to estimate a new instance's relationship to the classes. Reported applications include machinery failure detection, MRI tissue classification, automotive-engine fault recognition, battery state-of-charge estimation, and incomplete survey data. When applying it, the inputs, class definitions, and treatment of incomplete records need to be made explicit so that classifications can be evaluated consistently.
tiers.paperLevel: An ENN is a hybrid pattern-recognition classifier: ENN = artificial neural network + extension theory. The neural network provides fast, adaptive learning, while extension theory provides correlation estimation through the calculation of extension distance for classifying instances. M. H. Wang and C. P. Hung introduced the method in 2003.

explainer.example: For MRI tissue classification, an ENN would learn from the available MRI data, calculate extension distance for a new tissue instance, and use the estimated class relationship to assign that instance to a tissue category.

components.name: Data set
components.detail: Provides the instances that the network learns from and classifies.

components.name: Artificial neural network
components.detail: Contributes fast, adaptive learning of patterns in the data.

components.name: Extension-distance calculation
components.detail: Applies extension theory to estimate correlations between instances and classes.

components.name: Classification output
components.detail: Assigns each input instance to a recognized category.

flow: Instances from the data set enter the architecture.
The artificial neural network adaptively learns their patterns.
Extension distance is calculated to estimate correlations with possible classes.
The resulting relationship is used to classify the instance.
explainer.origin: M. H. Wang and C. P. Hung introduced the extension neural network in 2003 as a method for classifying instances in data sets.
explainer.lineage: ENN is a hybrid of artificial neural networks and extension theory, combining neural-network learning with correlation estimation based on extension distance.
explainer.whyItMatters: The architecture shows how two different approaches can be combined for classification: one learns adaptively from data, while the other estimates relationships to classes. Its reported uses span industrial diagnostics, medical imaging, energy systems, and incomplete survey data.
